item.text: {"text":"The closest direct precedent is older than the requested window: [MTAM, CIKM 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) introduces temporal gates into recurrent state transitions and attention, using a time-aware GRU to represent short-term intent. Recent related work includes [GRU-based session-aware recommendation (2024)](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-5903/16/2/51), which explores latent interaction integration with GRUs and attention, and [DICSI (2025)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-025-00650-w), which models changing session intent through temporal convolutions and adaptive attention. These support investigating dynamic intent, but do not establish that elapsed-time gaps identify intent changes or that learned GRU resets outperform fixed recent-history pooling.\n\nA concrete hypothesis derived from these results: jointly learn a retention gate from log-transformed inter-event gaps, the current item embedding and the previous hidden state, then feed the gated state into the GRU. Content dependence could preserve relevant history across long gaps while allowing rapid intent changes within short gaps; this remains an experimental proposal. Compare against a parameter-matched, time-blind GRU in separate trials, retaining one trained model per category. Use only observed history timestamps, mask padding updates, read the final nonpadding position, and reproduce timestamp handling in inference. Evaluate with the fixed macro validation HR@10; inspect retention versus gap length and item continuity as diagnostics, without treating inferred boundaries as observed intent labels."}
